packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, fresh subagent, prompt and images only; repository and search tools available but forbidden; exposures stated in each response
text:
PACKET-13 - unverified image-only reading

Exposure statement
- Nothing in my context before reading (task instructions, PROMPT.md) proposed an identification or reading of this fragment. It is a blind reading in that sense.
- I did nothing beyond the stated rules, with one exception. To read the small script, I made 2x enlarged crops of image-002, -003, -005 and -006 with PIL in my own scratch directory and viewed them. These crops contain no content beyond the supplied images. I also ran one `ls` on the packet directories to get the filenames. I did not open packet.json.

Images
- image-001.jpg: overview of face labelled in pencil "Stams, STA, Frg. 149r".
- image-002 (left half) and image-003 (right half): overlapping native tiles of that face. The left column of image-003 repeats the right part of image-002.
- image-004.jpg: overview of the other face, labelled "Stams, STA, Frg. 149v".
- image-005 (left) and image-006 (right): overlapping tiles of 149v.
- All images loaded.

Layout survey (observations)
- Single strip, about 15 x 6 cm, landscape. The text occupies only the top third, with 8 lines per column. Below it is a large blank band, which looks like a lower page margin. The top edge cuts close to or through the first line.
- Two columns of text per face. A dark vertical crease or stain runs near the intercolumn space. On 149r the crease lies under the right part of column a.
- Small Gothic textualis with heavy abbreviation, brown ink, now faded on 149v.
- Red initials begin new entries. Some are large (2 lines high, hanging partly into the margin) and some are one line high inside a line. There are red touches or strokes on some letters.
- Marginal words in a similar hand, brown ink, sit beside the columns: left margin of 149r col a ("Asplaltu" with red A); right margin of 149r col b ("Coredula(?)", "O?usat", "Corrigiola"); right margin of 149v col b ("Co..s", "...niu", "kurkenbo..."). Several of these appear to repeat the word that opens an entry nearby in the column, i.e. headword-like marginal finding words (interpretation).
- Further faded or ghost writing is visible in the left margin of 149r (about 4 lines under "Asplaltu") and in the top-right corner of 149v. It is unread.
- Tentative interpretation: a text of short entries, each opening with a red initial and a keyword, followed by definitions using "d(icitu)r", "i(d est)", "ul'(uel)". Source tags such as "ysid' eth'" and "in hystoria sup(er) lib(rum)..." appear inside entries. No lemma/commentary split is visible beyond this.

Spans selected: all 8 lines of both columns on both faces (32 lines). Many words in them are only partly read. Unread: the faded marginal ghost writing. A UV or raking-light image of 149v col b and of the 149r left margin would help.

Conventions: () expansion; [..] lost or unread letters; ? uncertain; (red X) red initial. Letter-by-letter renderings in quotes are given where I cannot make a word. Line numbers count from the top text line of the strip; the text block is at the top of each image.

Limitations
- Only 8 lines per column survive, and the top line is clipped by the upper cut edge on both faces.
- 149v col b is pale and abraded, and the large red initials there are flaked away. Their letter forms are uncertain.
- Many abbreviations and some whole words in 149r col a l.4-8 are uncertain. In particular the red mid-line initials there are faint, so the entry boundaries in col a are not secure.
- The column order on each face is clear: the columns sit side by side. Which face was originally the recto is taken from the pencil labels only.
- Suggested additional imaging: UV of 149v col b and of the marginal ghost writing on 149r (left) and 149v (top right).
